instruction: Ronald has sent me a message on phone regarding some amazon order. I am forgetting the details. Do as requested as per their last message.
notes: Flow: read passwords, log into phone, look up Ronald's contact (phone number + email), read his latest text (reveals product and quantity, shipping to supervisor's home, and the request to be paid back via Venmo). Then on Amazon: resolve the product id by searching the product name, clear the cart so the order contains exactly the requested items (CartEntry changes are ignored by the evaluation), add the requested quantity, look up the home address id and a payment card id, place the order, and read the order total via show_order. Finally request that total from Ronald's email on Venmo and complete the task. The gmail changes in the evaluation (order confirmation email with receipt attachment) are produced automatically by Amazon when the order is placed, so no gmail calls are modeled. Assumption: the message requests a single product/quantity; if several products are requested, amazon-add-product-to-cart is simply repeated per product (the model would need one product/quantity pair per item). Hidden world facts (contact phone/email, requested product/quantity, order total) are static init facts gated by knowledge predicates set by the lookup actions; goal correctness (right product, quantity, home address, recipient and amount) is enforced structurally through action preconditions, so the goal only needs the order and payment-request records plus task-completed.
